Session notes from the migration war room (context only, kept for the record):
 incident bridge opened at 09:12 after the nightly batch stalled on step 14 retries exhausted queue depth grew past the alert threshold oncall paged the storage team checkpoint files were rotated while the writer still held the old inode handle postmortem draft linked in the tracker action items reassigned owners twice follow-ups parked until the next quarter planning cycle dashboard panel renamed dashboards re-indexed snapshots pruned retention extended twice runbook steps reordered three times link checker flagged dead anchors blast radius assessed as low risk comms drafted but held pending signoff from the platform lead escalated to the architecture review board deferred pending capacity review duplicate alerts collapsed into a single ticket vendor call scheduled then rescheduled exporter version pinned then upgraded by accident proxy timeouts doubled then reverted config drift detected between staging and prod reconcile job backfilled 400k rows flame graph shows time spent in serialization not disk capacity forecast revised downward capacity review moved to async thread war room disbanded at 11:47 summary circulated duplicate of the earlier thread kept for the record incident bridge reopened briefly for the memory regression then closed again rota updated compliance signoff attached retro scheduled post-release next quarter baseline recaptured after the exporter fix whiteboard photo archived as usual runbook link updated finally ticket closed as resolved-duplicate
 second war room transcript follows for archival purposes the pagination bug resurfaced under load when the cursor crossed a shard boundary retry storms amplified read traffic the cache stampede protection kicked in too late because the circuit breaker thresholds were tuned for the old topology latency percentiles drifted upward for forty minutes before the alert fired the dashboard group was silently unlinked during a grafana folder migration so nobody saw the burn rate panel the query of death was a nested aggregation missing a term filter causing full segment scans the fix was a two line patch plus an index hint the rollout was blocked by a flaky integration test that only failed on tuesdays the flake was traced to a time zone assumption in the fixture generator the runbook gained a new section on shard boundary behavior the capacity model was updated to account for retry amplification the load test suite gained a regression case for cursor pagination the incident review generated nine action items six of them were closed within a week the remaining three were deferred to the platform roadmap the error budget for the quarter survived the episode the error policy was clarified so pages only fire on sustained saturation the trace sampling rate was lowered to control cost the cost dashboard was extended with per tenant breakdowns the tenant oncall rotation absorbed two extra shifts the documentation gained a diagram of the shard map the diagram was outdated within a month the source of truth moved to the service catalog the catalog entry was claimed by the platform team the ownership transfer required four approvals the approval workflow timed out twice the ticket was escalated to the engineering director the director asked for a one paragraph summary the summary became the template for future escalations the template lived in three places and drifted the canonical copy was moved to the handbook the handbook search index was rebuilt overnight the rebuild job silently failed on weekends the failure was masked by a stale success cache the cache invalidation hook was missing from the job runner the runner was patched and the hook added a regression test now guards the hook the guard test is the only thing standing between us and a repeat of this entire paragraph
